title: A state spent a year asking to be renamed. Parliament finally said yes on this day. November 22, 2026.
excerpt: Tamil Nadu's renaming bill, an Indian-origin economist's new role at the Asian Development Bank, a record month for foreign investment in Indian stocks, and a founder giving away 100,000 pairs of glasses.
bodyHtml:
A state spent a year asking to be renamed. Parliament finally said yes on this day

On November 22, 1968, the Lok Sabha passed the Madras State (Alteration of Name) Bill, renaming Madras State to Tamil Nadu. The change began with the state assembly's unanimous resolution in July 1967, and Parliament's passage of the bill in November 1968 cleared the way for the new name to formally take effect in January 1969.

He grew up in India, taught at Harvard - and just became one of Asia's top economists

Karthik Muralidharan was named Chief Economist and Director General at the Asian Development Bank on November 18, 2026. Muralidharan grew up in India before earning degrees at Harvard and Cambridge, and currently holds the Tata Chancellor's Professorship in Economics at UC San Diego. He founded the Centre for Effective Governance of Indian States, which partners directly with Indian state governments on policy delivery - experience he'll now bring to ADB's Asia-Pacific research starting July 2027.

Foreign investors just poured a record amount into Indian stocks in a single month

Foreign Portfolio Investors poured Rs 99,158 crore into Indian equities this November (through Nov 18 alone) - the highest monthly FPI inflow into Indian equities on record, surpassing the previous record of $8.4 billion set in December 2020. NSDL data shows over a trillion rupees in net inflows between late October and mid-November, with financials and auto stocks drawing the most money.

A year after taking his company public, he's giving away 100,000 pairs of glasses

Lenskart co-founder Peyush Bansal marked one year since the company's IPO by saying "what we have done is not enough." This November, Lenskart made blue-light filtering lenses a standard, no-extra-charge feature across its India stores, and pledged free glasses - frame plus prescription lenses, just a Rs 199 fitting fee - for the first 100,000 eligible children aged 5-12, with free eye tests for ages 8-12, timed to India's Children's Day.

Four stories today, one thread: institutions, people, and companies that keep showing up to do the specific, unglamorous work of building something real.
